question: Pongal, a harvest festival is dedicated to the __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun God.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__****Pongal**

__
 
• **Pongal is a harvest festiva**l celebrated by the **Tamil community.**
 
• It is a celebration **to thank the Sun, Mother Nature and the various farm animals** that help to contribute to a bountiful harvest.
 
• **Celebrated over four days**, Pongal also marks the **beginning of the Tamil month called Thai**, which is considered an auspicious month.
 
• It usually falls on the **14th or 15th of January each year.**
 
• Pongal is also the name of the dish made and eaten during this festival. It is a mixture of boiled sweet rice.
 
• It is **derived from the Tamil word pongu**, which means **“to boil over”**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vasant Panchami**, also called Saraswati Puja in honor of the **Hindu goddess Saraswati.**
 
• It is a festival that marks the preparation for the arrival of spring.
 
• The festival is celebrated by people of Dharmic religions in the Indian subcontinent and Nepal in different ways depending on the region.
 
• A festival essentially dedicated to the **fire and the sun God, Lohri **is associated with the concept of life and health in the Hindu religion.
 
• **Ganga Dussehra **is one of the major festivals observed in India** in the honor of Goddess Ganga.**
 
• It is celebrated on the tenth day of the Shukla Paksha (waxing Moon) of the Jyestha month, as per the Hindu calendar
